content: Do not praise the day until the evening has settled; do not praise a sword until it has been tested in battle.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: At kveldi skal dag lofa (Hávamál, Stanza 81) — Poetic Edda
explanation: The morning sun may dawn clear and bright, only for an afternoon blizzard to strike. The polished sword may look glittering on the wall, only to snap against iron armor. Suspend premature bragging; judge things by how they conclude, not by how they begin.
practicalInsight: Refrain from premature celebration on an unfinished project today. See it through to the final, quiet completion.
reflectionPrompt: Where have you celebrated early only to stumble before the finish line?
